chapter: Bird's world, singers and the new music
title: McGhee's sunglasses
summary: He wore dark glasses because of sensitive eyes.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: The first images I had of you at the time of Jazz at The Philharmonic, that record we talked about before that put Jazz At the Philharmonic on the map...
...and the Dial records. Here was the slim, handsome
guy with the dark glasses on. You had those certain kind of sunglasses that you wore which were different than what the other guys were wearing.

Yeah. Well, most people didn't realize that I had sensitive eyes. I couldn't go on the stage with them bright lights shining down in my face, and not have on dark glasses, because I'd get the damnedest headaches I ever had in my life behind them bright lights! And my eyes are very sensitive, so I had to wear dark glasses in order to do that.

Especially, like... When I was playing with Barnet, boy, I think they had the brightest lights in the world up there, man, in the picture booths... And when they used to throw that bright light on me, man... I don't know, maybe they were trying to make me look White or something! But they sure had bright lights on me.
Well, the pictures I remember were not necessarily indoor. There were outdoor pictures and you were wearing your glasses...

Of course, the fashion had been in Jazz circles a little before with those Air Corps type sunglasses -- people used to be wearing those. And then of course, Dizzy came along with the heavy rims, which they tell me Monk really
originated. And then yours seemed to be the rimless...
Let me show some pictures I have here.
We'll look at them in a minute...
